title: Mono-phosphorylation at Ser4 of Barrier-to-autointegration Factor (Banf1) significantly reduces its DNA binding capability by inducing critical changes in its local conformation and DNA binding surface
authors: Ming Tang; Amila Suraweera; Xuqiang Nie; Zilin Li; James W. Wells; Kenneth J O’Byrne; Robert J Woods; Emma Bolderson; Derek J Richard
one_liner_zh: 该文通过分子建模与MD模拟研究Banf1磷酸化对蛋白-DNA结合能力的影响，属于广义蛋白-DNA互作机制研究，方法可迁移至TF-DNA体系，但对象非典型TF-DNA。
abstract: Barrier-to-Autointegration Factor (Banf1) is a small DNA-bridging protein. The binding status of Banf1 to DNA is regulated by its N-terminal phosphorylation and dephosphorylation, which plays a critical role in cell proliferation. Banf1 can be phosphorylated at Ser4 into mono-phosphorylated Banf1, which is further phosphorylated at Thr3 to form di-phosphorylated Banf1. It was observed decades ago that mono-phosphorylated Banf1 cannot bind to DNA. However, the underlying molecular- and atomic-level mechanisms remain unclear. A clear understanding of these mechanisms will aid in interfering with the cell proliferation process for better global health. Herein, we explored the detailed atomic bases of unphosphorylated Banf1-DNA binding and how mono- and di-phosphorylation of Banf1 impair these atomic bases to eliminate its DNA-binding capability, followed by exploring the DNA-binding capability of mono- and di-phosphorylation Banf1, using comprehensive and systematic molecular modelling and molecular dynamics simulations. This work presented in detail the residue-level binding energies, hydrogen bonds and water bridges between Banf1 and DNA, some of which have not been reported. Moreover, we revealed that mono-phosphorylation of Banf1 causes its N-terminal secondary structure changes, which in turn induce significant changes in Banf1’s DNA binding surface, thus eliminating its DNA-binding capability. At the atomic level, we also uncovered the alterations in interactions due to the induction of mono-phosphorylation that result in the N-terminal secondary structure changes of Banf1. Additionally, our modelling showed that phosphorylated Banf1 with their dominant N-terminal secondary structures bind to DNA with a significantly lower affinity and the docked binding pose are not stable in MD simulations. These findings help future studies in predicting effect of mutations in Banf1 on its DNA-binding capability and open a novel avenue for the development of therapeutics such as cancer drugs, targeting cell proliferation by inducing conformational changes in Banf1’s N-terminal domain.
abstract_zh: 屏障自身整合因子（Barrier-to-Autointegration Factor, Banf1）是一种小型DNA桥接蛋白。Banf1与DNA的结合状态受其N端磷酸化和去磷酸化的调控，这对细胞增殖至关重要。Banf1可在Ser4位点被磷酸化形成单磷酸化Banf1，随后在Thr3位点进一步磷酸化形成双磷酸化Banf1。数十年前已观察到单磷酸化Banf1无法与DNA结合，但其分子及原子层面的机制尚不清楚。清晰理解这些机制将有助于干预细胞增殖过程，从而促进全球健康。在此，我们利用全面系统的分子建模和分子动力学（molecular dynamics）模拟，探讨了未磷酸化Banf1与DNA结合的详细原子基础，以及单磷酸化和双磷酸化如何破坏这些原子基础以消除其DNA结合能力，并进一步探究了单磷酸化和双磷酸化Banf1的DNA结合能力。本研究详细呈现了Banf1与DNA之间的残基级结合能、氢键和水桥，其中部分信息此前未见报道。此外，我们揭示单磷酸化导致Banf1的N端二级结构变化，进而引起Banf1 DNA结合表面的显著改变，从而消除其DNA结合能力。在原子层面，我们还揭示了由单磷酸化诱导的相互作用变化，这些变化导致Banf1的N端二级结构改变。另外，我们的建模显示，具有主导N端二级结构的磷酸化Banf1与DNA结合亲和力显著降低，且对接的结合姿态在分子动力学模拟中不稳定。这些发现有助于未来研究预测Banf1突变对其DNA结合能力的影响，并为开发靶向细胞增殖的疗法（如癌症药物）开辟新途径，通过诱导Banf1 N端结构域的构象变化来实现。
